'''Sylvie Roke''' (born 1977 in [[De Bilt]], [[Netherlands]]) is a Dutch chemist and physicist specialized in [[photonics]] and aqueous systems. As a full professor she holds Julia Jacobi Chair of Photomedicine at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and is the director of the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Welcome to LBP!|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lbp/|access-date=2021-03-15|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Roke studied in Utrecht, graduating from [[Utrecht University]] with degrees in chemistry (1995-2000, highest honors) and experimental physics (1997-2000, highest honors). She joined Aart W. Kleyn's Molecular Beams Group at the Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics ([[AMOLF]]) to work on her extended master research project studying the interactions of small molecules with metal surfaces under ultrahigh vacuum conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Roke|first1=S.|last2=Coquel|first2=J.M.|last3=Kleyn|first3=A.W.|date=June 2000|title=The adsorption behaviour of isobutane on Pt(533): A combined RAIRS and TPD study|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0009261400005285|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|language=en|volume=323|issue=3–4|pages=201–208|doi=10.1016/S0009-2614(00)00528-5|bibcode=2000CPL...323..201R |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Sylvie Roke|url=https://people.epfl.ch/sylvie.roke/?lang=en|website=EPFL}}</ref> Alfons van Blaaderen (chemistry) and [[Albert Polman]] (physics) where her thesis supervisors from Utrecht University. She continued as a PhD student in the Kleyn group moving to [[Leiden University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Roke|first1=Sylvie|last2=Kleyn|first2=Aart W|last3=Bonn|first3=Mischa|date=March 2003|title=Time- vs. frequency-domain femtosecond surface sum frequency generation|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S000926140300085X|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|language=en|volume=370|issue=1–2|pages=227–232|doi=10.1016/S0009-2614(03)00085-X|bibcode=2003CPL...370..227R |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2004, she graduated with highest honors with thesis co-supervised by Mischa Bonn on "New light on hidden surfaces."<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=New light on hidden surfaces|url=https://www.differ.nl/node/1295|publisher=Leiden University|date=2004|place=Leiden, Netherlands|first=S.|last=Roke}}</ref>

As a postdoctoral student she joined first the FOM Institute for Plasma Physics in [[Nieuwegein]], and thereafter she worked as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]] with Michael Grunze at the Institute of Applied Physical Chemistry at [[Heidelberg University]]. In 2005, enabled by a Floating Research Group Leader position and the opportunity to set up her own laboratory from the [[Max Planck Society|Max-Planck Society]], she moved to the [[Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems|Max Planck Institute for Metals Research]] in [[Stuttgart]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dadap|first1=Jerry I.|last2=de Aguiar|first2=Hilton B.|last3=Roke|first3=Sylvie|date=2009-06-07|title=Nonlinear light scattering from clusters and single particles|url=http://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.3141383|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=130|issue=21|page=214710|doi=10.1063/1.3141383|pmid=19508090 |bibcode=2009JChPh.130u4710D |issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Diving into surfaces|url=https://www.mpg.de/277058/Sylvie_Roke|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref>

In 2011, she joined  [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] first as an [[assistant professor]] and was promoted as full professor in 2015.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=14 new professors at the two Federal Institutes of Technology {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/14-professorinnen-und-professoren-den-beiden-eth-ernannt|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.ethrat.ch}}</ref> She is the holder of the Julia Jacobi Chair in Photomedicine, and the director of the Laboratory for fundamental BioPhotonics with affiliations both at the Institutes of Bioengineering and Materials (IMX) at the Schools of Engineering and of Life Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Institute of Bioengineering|url=https://www.epfl.ch/research/domains/bioengineering/|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Materials - STI - School of Engineering|url=https://sti.epfl.ch/research/institutes/imx/|access-date=2021-03-22|website=sti.epfl.ch}}</ref> In 2021, she became the director of the Institute of Bioengineering.<ref>{{Cite web|institution=Institute of Bioengineering, EPFL|last=Reinhard|first=Dietrich|date=2021-01-02|title=New Directors' Tandem Heading the EPFL's Institute of Bioengineering|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/new-directors-tandem-heading-the-epfl-s-institute-/|language=en}}</ref> In 2022, she got the [[Optica (society)|Optica]] Fellow "For pioneering contributions to the theory and practice of nonlinear light scattering and imaging technologies that enable molecular level studies of complex aqueous solutions ".<ref name="optica.org">{{Cite web |title=Fellows Search {{!}} Awards & Honors {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/fellows_search/ |access-date=2023-06-26 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

== Research ==

Roke performs theoretical research and develops non-invasive label-free optical tools for the probing of aqueous systems and interfaces. Her research aims at understanding the properties of water on molecular level in diverse systems such as in aqueous electrolyte and polyelectrolyte solutions, at buried interfaces, in and outside droplets, in curved nanoscale and microscale membranes, in pores and in living cells such as neurons.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Okur|first1=Halil I.|last2=Tarun|first2=Orly B.|last3=Roke|first3=Sylvie|date=2019-07-19|title=Chemistry of Lipid Membranes from Models to Living Systems: A Perspective of Hydration, Surface Potential, Curvature, Confinement and Heterogeneity|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=141|issue=31|pages=12168–12181|doi=10.1021/jacs.9b02820|pmid=31323177 |s2cid=207196344 |issn=0002-7863}}</ref>

To elucidate molecular surface structures, morphologies and chirality of nano- and microscopic objects in solutions, Roke invented vibrational sum frequency scattering (SFS), a method that allows the recording the vibrational spectrum of the molecular interfacial layer around objects.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Roke|first=Sylvie|date=2009-07-13|title=Nonlinear Optical Spectroscopy of Soft Matter Interfaces|journal=ChemPhysChem|volume=10|issue=9–10|pages=1380–1388|doi=10.1002/cphc.200900138|pmid=19472266 |issn=1439-4235}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=de Aguiar|first1=Hilton B.|last2=Samson|first2=Jean-Sebastien|last3=Roke|first3=Sylvie|date=April 2012|title=Erratum to: ''Probing nanoscopic droplet interfaces in aqueous solution with vibrational sum-frequency scattering: A study of the effects of path length, droplet density and pulse energy'' [Chem. Phys. Lett. 512 (2011) 7680]|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|volume=531|page=275|doi=10.1016/j.cplett.2012.01.055|bibcode=2012CPL...531..275D |issn=0009-2614|doi-access=free}}</ref> She used SFS to specify the molecular interfaces of [[complex system]]s:<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Johnson|first1=Mark A.|title=Annual review of physical chemistry. Volume 63, 2012|last2=Martinez|first2=Todd J.|last3=Cremer|first3=Paul S.|last4=Groves|first4=Jay T.|date=2012|publisher=Annual Reviews|isbn=978-0-8243-1063-9|location=Palo Alto, Calif.|oclc=819747683}}</ref> polymer particles in a solid matrix, particles in solution, oil droplets in water (emulsions),<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zdrali|first1=Evangelia|last2=Chen|first2=Yixing|last3=Okur|first3=Halil I.|last4=Wilkins|first4=David M.|last5=Roke|first5=Sylvie|date=2017-12-14|title=The Molecular Mechanism of Nanodroplet Stability|journal=ACS Nano|volume=11|issue=12|pages=12111–12120|doi=10.1021/acsnano.7b05100|pmid=29224343 |issn=1936-0851}}</ref> lipid droplet like systems,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Yixing|last2=Jena|first2=Kailash C.|last3=Lütgebaucks|first3=Cornelis|last4=Okur|first4=Halil I.|last5=Roke|first5=Sylvie|date=2015-07-10|title=Three Dimensional Nano "Langmuir Trough" for Lipid Studies|journal=Nano Letters|volume=15|issue=8|pages=5558–5563|doi=10.1021/acs.nanolett.5b02143|pmid=26151602 |bibcode=2015NanoL..15.5558C |issn=1530-6984}}</ref> water droplets,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Smolentsev|first1=Nikolay|last2=Smit|first2=Wilbert J.|last3=Bakker|first3=Huib J.|last4=Roke|first4=Sylvie|date=2017-05-24|title=The interfacial structure of water droplets in a hydrophobic liquid|journal=Nature Communications|volume=8|issue=1|article-number=15548 |doi=10.1038/ncomms15548|pmid=28537259 |pmc=5458086 |bibcode=2017NatCo...815548S |issn=2041-1723|doi-access=free}}</ref> a micro-jet and liposomes in aqueous solution. Her studies indicate that objects on nano- and microscale show different behaviors as model planar interfaces.

Roke has also developed high throughput polarimetric angle resolved second harmonic scattering (AR-SHS), a method allowing for probing particle interfaces and liquids.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gomopoulos|first1=Nikolaos|last2=Lütgebaucks|first2=Cornelis|last3=Sun|first3=Qinchao|last4=Macias-Romero|first4=Carlos|last5=Roke|first5=Sylvie|date=2013-01-08|title=Label-free second harmonic and hyper Rayleigh scattering with high efficiency|journal=Optics Express|volume=21|issue=1|pages=815–821|doi=10.1364/oe.21.000815|pmid=23388974 |bibcode=2013OExpr..21..815G |issn=1094-4087|doi-access=free}}</ref> Making use of non-resonant second harmonic response of water and its response to electrostatic fields, Roke developed a method to determine the surface potential from particle interfaces and the amount of oriented water.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lütgebaucks|first1=Cornelis|last2=Gonella|first2=Grazia|last3=Roke|first3=Sylvie|date=2016-11-10|title=Optical label-free and model-free probe of the surface potential of nanoscale and microscopic objects in aqueous solution|journal=Physical Review B|volume=94|issue=19|article-number=195410 |doi=10.1103/physrevb.94.195410|bibcode=2016PhRvB..94s5410L |issn=2469-9950}}</ref>The technique has been used to measure the direct interaction of [[Pore-forming toxin|pore-forming toxins]] such as perfringolysin O<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schönfeldová |first=T. |last2=Okur |first2=H. I. |last3=Vezočnik |first3=V. |last4=Iacovache |first4=I. |last5=Cao |first5=C. |last6=Dal Peraro |first6=M. |last7=Maček |first7=P. |last8=Zuber |first8=B. |last9=Roke |first9=S. |date=2022-04-14 |title=Ultrasensitive Label-Free Detection of Protein–Membrane Interaction Exemplified by Toxin-Liposome Insertion |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c04011 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters |volume=13 |issue=14 |pages=3197–3201 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c04011|pmc=9014461 }}</ref> and [[aerolysin]]<ref>Roesel, T., Cao, C., Bada Juarez, J. F., Dal Peraro, M. & Roke, S. [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c00035 Dissecting the Membrane Association Mechanism of Aerolysin Pores at Femtomolar Concentrations Using Water as a Probe]. ''Nano Lett'' '''24''', 13888–13894 (2024). doi: https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.nanolett.4c00035</ref> with [[Liposome|liposomes]]. 

By investigating aqueous solutions, she discovered long-range interactions of ions and water that stem from the influence of the ionic [[Electric field|electrostatic field]] on the water-water [[hydrogen bond]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Yixing|last2=Okur|first2=Halil I.|last3=Gomopoulos|first3=Nikolaos|last4=Macias-Romero|first4=Carlos|last5=Cremer|first5=Paul S.|last6=Petersen|first6=Poul B.|last7=Tocci|first7=Gabriele|last8=Wilkins|first8=David M.|last9=Liang|first9=Chungwen|last10=Ceriotti|first10=Michele|last11=Roke|first11=Sylvie|date=April 2016|title=Electrolytes induce long-range orientational order and free energy changes in the H-bond network of bulk water|journal=Science Advances|volume=2|issue=4|article-number=e1501891|doi=10.1126/sciadv.1501891|pmid=27152357 |pmc=4846452 |bibcode=2016SciA....2E1891C |issn=2375-2548|doi-access=free}}</ref> Roke found that these interactions are amplified in viscoelastic liquids made of polyelectrolytes such [[Hyaluronan]], and furthermore correlate with the viscosity of such liquids.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dedic|first1=J.|last2=Okur|first2=H. I.|last3=Roke|first3=S.|date=December 2019|title=Polyelectrolytes induce water-water correlations that result in dramatic viscosity changes and nuclear quantum effects|journal=Science Advances|language=en|volume=5|issue=12|article-number=eaay1443|doi=10.1126/sciadv.aay1443|pmid=32064319 |pmc=6989307|bibcode=2019SciA....5.1443D |issn=2375-2548|doi-access=free}}</ref> She developed [[Wide-field multiphoton microscopy|high-throughput wide field multiphoton microscopy]] with an about thousand fold increased signal to noise ratio when compared to standard multiphoton confocal imaging systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Macias-Romero|first1=Carlos|last2=Nahalka|first2=Igor|last3=Okur|first3=Halil I.|last4=Roke|first4=Sylvie|date=2017-07-20|title=Optical imaging of surface chemistry and dynamics in confinement|journal=Science|volume=357|issue=6353|pages=784–788|doi=10.1126/science.aal4346|pmid=28729352 |issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free|arxiv=1707.00590}}</ref> A further advantage of this method is a reduction of the photodamage effect in living cells.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Macias-Romero|first1=C.|last2=Zubkovs|first2=V.|last3=Wang|first3=S.|last4=Roke|first4=S.|date=2016-03-24|title=Wide-field medium-repetition-rate multiphoton microscopy reduces photodamage of living cells|journal=Biomedical Optics Express|volume=7|issue=4|pages=1458–1467|doi=10.1364/boe.7.001458|pmid=27446668 |pmc=4929654 |issn=2156-7085|doi-access=free}}</ref> This allows for the spatiotemporal imaging of interfacial water in various systems: imaging water undergoing surface chemical reactions, electro-catalysis,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zwaschka|first1=Gregor|last2=Nahalka|first2=Igor|last3=Marchioro|first3=Arianna|last4=Tong|first4=Yujin|last5=Roke|first5=Sylvie|last6=Campen|first6=R. Kramer|date=2020-04-30|title=Imaging the Heterogeneity of the Oxygen Evolution Reaction on Gold Electrodes Operando: Activity is Highly Local|journal=ACS Catalysis|volume=10|issue=11|pages=6084–6093|doi=10.1021/acscatal.0c01177|pmid=32551180 |pmc=7295367|issn=2155-5435|doi-access=free}}</ref> membrane water and the restructuring of water inside ion channels<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tarun|first1=Orly B.|last2=Eremchev|first2=Maksim Yu.|last3=Radenovic|first3=Aleksandra|last4=Roke|first4=Sylvie|date=2019-10-03|title=Spatiotemporal Imaging of Water in Operating Voltage-Gated Ion Channels Reveals the Slow Motion of Interfacial Ions|journal=Nano Letters|volume=19|issue=11|pages=7608–7613|doi=10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b02024|pmid=31580677 |bibcode=2019NanoL..19.7608T |s2cid=203661186 |issn=1530-6984}}</ref> and activated living mammalian neurons. The latter enables a new way of measuring membrane potentials and ion fluxes in neurons using water as a probe.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Didier|first1=M. E. P.|last2=Tarun|first2=O. B.|last3=Jourdain|first3=P.|last4=Magistretti|first4=P.|last5=Roke|first5=S.|date=December 2018|title=Membrane water for probing neuronal membrane potentials and ionic fluxes at the single cell level|journal=Nature Communications|volume=9|issue=1|page=5287 |doi=10.1038/s41467-018-07713-w|pmid=30538243 |pmc=6289965 |bibcode=2018NatCo...9.5287D |issn=2041-1723|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
Roke is the winner for several [[European Research Council|ERC]] grants: ERC Synergy Grant (2020; with Aurélien Roux, [[University of Geneva]]),<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERC-Grant-Roux-Roke|url=https://nccr-chembio.ch/news/erc-grant-roux-roke/erc-grant-roux-roke-2/|access-date=2021-03-23|website=NCCR in Chemical Biology|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Zoom sur les flux d'eau cellulaires-Brèves-Lʹisolement en psychiatrie-La fabrication du vin sous surveillance chimique - Radio|url=https://www.rts.ch/play/radio/cqfd/audio/zoom-sur-les-flux-deau-cellulaires-breves-lisolement-en-psychiatrie-la-fabrication-du-vin-sous-surveillance-chimique?id=11704065|access-date=2021-03-23|website=Play RTS| date=9 November 2020 |language=fr}}</ref> ERC Proof of Concept Grant (2020), ERC Consolidator Grant (2014), ERC Starting Grant (2009)

She is an elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS; 2020)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home - Unit - DCP|url=https://engage.aps.org/dcp/home|access-date=2021-03-23|website=engage.aps.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|institution=Basic Sciences, EPFL|last=Papageorgiou|first=Nik|date=2020-01-10|title=Suliana Manley and Sylvie Roke elected APS Fellows|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/suliana-manley-and-sylvie-roke-elected-aps-fello-3/|language=en}}</ref> and of [[Optica (society)|OPTICA]] (2022).<ref name="optica.org"/> She is a fellow of the Young Academy of the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2010) and the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|German Academy of Natural Scientists, Leopoldina]] (2010), a young fellow at the [[Werner von Siemens Ring]], and was selected for the Excellence Network of the [[Robert Bosch Stiftung|Robert-Bosch Foundation]].

She is the recipient of the [[Hertha Sponer Prize]] of the [[German Physical Society]] (2008), the Minerva Prize by the ''Dutch Foundation for Fundamental Research on Matter'' (2006), and the L. J. Oosterhoff prize by the [[Leiden University]].

Roke has been involved in the creation of the start-up companies ORYL photonics<ref>{{Cite web|title=ORYL Photonics {{!}} Light for Life|url=https://www.orylphotonics.com/|access-date=2021-03-23|website=ORYL Photonics|language=en-US}}</ref> and Matis.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Startups developing a software to automate brain tumor detection, suspended drones for harvesting, innovative spinal care, an IR camera for authentication of artworks, and next generation cancer diagnostic and monitoring each win CHF 10,000|url=https://www.venturekick.ch/index.cfm?page=135333&article_id=4635|access-date=2021-03-23|website=www.venturekick.ch|language=en}}</ref>
